Develop and refine marketing strategy techniques.
Apply and expand personal project management knowledge and skills.
Deliver successful client project outcomes while optimizing time and resources to support company profitability.
Qualifications 3+ years of successful project experience; experience at a creative, marketing, or advertising agency is a plus.
Proven ability to collaborate with designers and work effectively within a creative process.
3+ years of hands‑on experience in email marketing, paid social, search marketing, and content management; experience with marketing automation is a strong plus.
Excellent copywriting skills (writing samples required during the interview process).
Proficiency with marketing, creative, and project management tools, including Mailchimp, Meta Business Suite, WordPress, Adobe Creative Suite, and Monday.
Strong communication skills with the ability to work cross‑functionally.
Highly detail‑oriented, organized, and capable of meeting deadlines.
Creative problem‑solver with a proactive approach to challenges.

# Office Manager

The Dreamer Group

[Los Angeles, CA](https://jooble.org/jobs/Los-Angeles%2C-CA)

[Apply](https://jooble.org/away/-6767724478441596040?p=1&pos=0&rgn=6546&pageType=7&jobAge=17758050&jdpSource=101&jdpid=4700515082423144774&crId=US_0US_0)

## Human Resource Manager

The Deamer Group is proud to partner with Black Women for Wellness in their search for a Human Resource Manager. This is a full-time opportunity located in Los Angeles, CA. Black Women for Wellness is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing policies and electing leaders who improve the health, well-being, and quality of life of Black women, girls, and gender expansive people.

Our work moves public policy forward, elects leaders who prioritize Black women's needs, shifts culture through media, and storytelling, and empowers community members to engage in the fight for equity and justice. Through organizing, advocacy, coalition building, and civic engagement, we are building political power that creates lasting systems change.

### Position Summary

The Office Manager is responsible for supporting the day-to-day administrative and operational functions of BWW to help ensure an organized, efficient, and well-functioning workplace. This role serves as a central point of coordination for office operations, administrative needs, internal processes, vendors, supplies, scheduling, and general staff support.

The Office Manager will work collaboratively across the organization to maintain effective office systems, coordinate operational activities, and ensure staff have the resources and support needed to perform their work effectively. The ideal candidate is highly organized, proactive, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities while providing responsive and professional support to staff, leadership, and external partners.

### Responsibilities and Tasks

- Manage the day-to-day operations of the office, maintaining an organized, professional, and welcoming environment that is clean, well-stocked, and ready for staff and visitors.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for office-related questions and requests, providing courteous, professional assistance to staff, leadership, visitors, vendors, and external partners.
- Manage office supplies, equipment, and inventory, including ordering, restocking, and coordinating repairs, maintenance, or replacement as needed.
- Serve as the primary liaison with building management on maintenance, repairs, access, and other facility needs, including managing keys, access cards, and parking information.
- Coordinate with office vendors and service providers, scheduling services, maintaining vendor records, and ensuring work is completed on time and to standard.
- Coordinate incoming and outgoing mail, packages, deliveries, and general office correspondence.
- Maintain organized electronic and physical files, records, and administrative documents, handling organizational and employee information with confidentiality and discretion.
- Maintain office calendars and manage shared spaces, conference rooms, and other workplace resources, including scheduling meetings, reserving rooms, and preparing meeting materials.
- Plan and coordinate logistics for in-person meetings, staff gatherings, trainings, and organizational events, including room setup and breakdown, catering, supplies, technology, and vendor coordination.
- Support employee onboarding and offboarding by preparing workspaces, coordinating equipment and office access, and helping new staff get oriented to the office and its resources.
- Collect, organize, and submit invoices, receipts, and support documentation for office purchases and services to the appropriate staff for processing and approval.
- Maintain records of office purchases, subscriptions, and vendor services, tracking recurring expenses, and anticipating upcoming office needs.
- Identify and recommend improvements to office organization, systems, and administrative processes to increase efficiency and better support staff.
- Provide general administrative support to staff and leadership, assist with special projects, and perform other related duties as assigned.

### Required Qualifications

- 3+ years of experience in office management, administrative support, or a similar role, including coordinating meetings, maintaining calendars, and supporting office events and activities.
- Strong organizational, time-management, and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain accurate records and documentation.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal, and customer-service skills, with the ability to work effectively with staff, leadership, visitors, vendors, and external partners.
- Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.
- Ability to work independently, take initiative, and anticipate and prioritize day-to-day office needs.
- Commitment to health equity, racial justice, gender justice, reproductive justice, and community-centered work.

### Valued and Preferred Experience

- Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Office Administration, or a related field.
- Experience in a nonprofit, advocacy, community-based, or mission-driven organization, supporting a team in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
- Experience coordinating vendors, facilities, supplies, and workplace services, including workspace, equipment, and office access for onboarding and offboarding.

Community Accountability - We honor our commitments to one another, our partners, and our community. We take ownership of our work, communicate with transparency, and follow through because our collective impact depends on each of us showing up with care and accountability.

Excellence in Action - We bring intention, consistency, and care to everything we do. We strive for high-quality work, embrace learning, and continuously strengthen our skills, so our programs, advocacy, and service reflect the excellence our community deserves.

Respectful Relationships - We cultivate trust by communicating with honesty, kindness, and respect. We address challenges directly, protect one another's dignity, avoid gossip and divisive behavior, and contribute to a workplace where everyone can thrive.

Collaboration for Collective Impact - We recognize that lasting change happens together. We value diverse perspectives, share knowledge generously, support one another across teams, and work in partnership to advance our mission and strengthen our community.

Mission-Centered Leadership - Regardless of title, we lead with integrity, courage, and a deep commitment to justice. We make decisions that reflect our values, center the well-being of Black women and girls, and contribute to building healthier, more equitable communities.

Black Women for Wellness is committed to building a workforce that reflects the communities we serve. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcome applicants of all backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, disability (physical or mental), medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, reproductive health decision-making, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

We will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with the California Fair Chance Act and applicable local laws.

Center For Rheumatology

Position Type: Full-Time, Exempt

Center for Rheumatology
Location: Encino, CA; onsite, with travel to our Los Angeles or North Hollywood locations as needed

Reports To: Director of Practice Operations

Direct Reports: All Encino site staff below the physicians, including front office, administrative, nursing, medical assistant, and imaging

Position Type: Full-Time, Exempt

Compensation: $70,000 to $110,000, based on experience

Position Overview
The Center for Rheumatology is one of Southern California's leading rheumatology practices, combining a busy multi-site clinical operation with an active research program of more than 25 ongoing clinical trials in lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and related conditions. We operate three Los Angeles area locations with approximately 40 staff and 11 providers, and we are growing through both new location launches and the acquisition of independent practices.

We are hiring an Office Manager to run our Encino location. You lead everyone at the site other than the physicians, front office and clinical staff alike, and you are accountable for how the whole site performs: patient flow, staffing, treatment readiness, and whether physicians spend their day practicing medicine rather than chasing the things around it. Encino is our smallest site, and we are looking for someone ready to take on a second location as the practice grows.

This is a working role. We are a 40-person practice, not a health system. On a short day you will check patients in or work a stuck authorization yourself. What sets this seat apart is what happens next: you find out why the day broke, fix the cause, and make sure it does not happen again.

We move quickly and run lean. The person closest to a problem is the one expected to solve it, and there is rarely a committee in between. Our CEO is a practicing rheumatologist who built this practice and still knows the operating detail at every site. The physicians here trust site leaders who fix things, and that trust is earned one fixed problem at a time.

What Success Looks Like In The First Year

Inside the first 60 days, you know Encino cold: the team, the workflows, where the day breaks down, and which fixes come first.

The site runs on written procedures the team actually uses, and no critical task depends on a single person.

Staff turnover is down, and you can explain why.

No patient arrives for an infusion or injection without an approved authorization and the medication on hand.

Patients leave with their next appointment booked, and you drive a regular review of the site scorecard.

Encino's patient volume is growing, backed by relationships you have built with referring practices and community partners.

Encino can run for a week without you. That is the test of readiness for a second site.

Key Responsibilities Leading the Team

Site leadership. Lead all site staff below the physicians. Set expectations, hold a regular cadence, coach, and address performance early and directly.

Clinical staff. Lead nurses, medical assistants, and imaging staff on scheduling, coverage, performance, and development, partnering with the physicians on clinical standards and California scope of practice.

Hiring and onboarding. Run hiring for site roles from requisition through offer, and onboard new staff to a written plan so they are productive in weeks rather than months.

Retention. Own turnover at the site. Know why people stay and why they leave, and act on it.

Employment practice. Keep the site compliant with California employment requirements: meal and rest periods, timekeeping, overtime, leave, and documentation.

Running the Site

Daily operations. Own patient flow from the first phone call through checkout, the daily huddle, staffing coverage, and the physical office.

Schedule and capacity. Maintain provider schedule templates, manage the schedule against physician and infusion chair capacity, smooth out arrival clustering, and backfill cancellations and no-shows.

Patient access and experience. Run call handling, callbacks, check-in, and follow‑up booking as measured functions with targets. Own complaints and service recovery, and elevate only what needs a physician or executive decision.

Physician partnership. Be the operational partner to the physicians at your site. Protect their time and take administrative work off their plate.

Treatment Readiness

Prior authorization at the site. Make sure every authorization has an owner, a status, and a follow‑up date, and that handoffs between front office, back office, and clinical staff hold. Escalate anything at risk of delaying treatment.

Infusion and biologic patients. Review upcoming patients on a set cadence so the authorization, the medication, and the chair are all in place before the patient arrives.

Supply and inventory. Execute CFR's receiving, counting, and storage standards at your site, in partnership with our Supply Chain and Procurement Manager, who owns purchasing and vendors.

Compliance, Numbers, and Systems

Compliance. Keep the site compliant with federal and California requirements, including the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) standards, and Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) requirements for the laboratory. Keep personnel, licensure, and training files ready for inspection.

Scorecard and budget. Own the site scorecard, including wait times, schedule utilization, call answer rates, authorization turnaround, follow‑up booking, and turnover, and manage the site's labor and operating spend within budget.

Systems. Be the site's power user for the electronic health record (EHR), practice management system, and patient portal. Train staff and move patient‑facing work into the portal instead of onto the phones.

Growth

Community and referral partners. Build relationships with referring physicians, local practices, and community organizations, and support the practice's marketing work for your site. Encino has room to grow, and you will be part of growing it.

Beyond Encino. Contribute to the standards CFR uses across sites, new locations, and acquired practices. As the practice grows, this role is expected to take on leadership of a second location.

Qualifications & Experience
Required

5+ years in physician practice or outpatient operations , including at least 3 years as an Office Manager, Practice Manager, Clinic Manager, or equivalent , personally accountable for a site: staffing, schedules, patient flow, and the problems that walk in the door.

Direct leadership of both administrative and clinical staff, with real ownership of hiring, performance management, and termination.

A track record of stabilizing a team or reducing turnover, with a specific account of what you did.

Hands‑on knowledge of prior authorization and how it affects treatment scheduling.

Advanced user of an EHR and practice management system, able to train others.

Working knowledge of HIPAA, OSHA, and California employment practice as it applies to a clinical workplace.

You drive accountability with data: you set targets with your team, track them on a scorecard, hold people to them, and own the result when the numbers slip.

Onsite five days a week in Encino, with reliable transportation for travel between our locations.

Strongly preferred

Specialty practice background where prior authorization, infusion, or in‑office drug administration is central: rheumatology, oncology, gastroenterology, neurology, dermatology, allergy and immunology.

Responsibility for more than one site at the same time, whether permanent or interim.

Oversight of in‑office ancillary services: infusion, laboratory, or imaging.

Nice to have

Bilingual English and Spanish.

Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, or a related field. Equivalent practical experience is also considered.

Certified Medical Practice Executive (CMPE) or a comparable practice management credential.

Experience being part of a new site opening or a practice acquisition.

This may not be the right fit if

Your experience is mostly running a front desk or a billing team. This seat leads a whole site, clinical staff included, and is measured on how that site performs.

You want one office that runs the same way every year. This role will grow and change as the practice does.

Additional Details

Travel: Based onsite in Encino, with travel to our Los Angeles or North Hollywood locations as needed.

Benefits: Health, dental and vision insurance, paid time off and paid sick leave, retirement plan

The Center for Rheumatology is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act.

# Administrative Coordinator

$23 - $27 per hour

Lunch Bunch

[Los Angeles, CA](https://jooble.org/jobs/Los-Angeles%2C-CA)

[Apply](https://jooble.org/away/2531042201571045476?p=1&pos=0&rgn=6546&pageType=7&jobAge=114&jdpSource=101&jdpid=-9208572861375809388&crId=US_0US_0)

Job Type

Part-time

Description

**About Lunch Bunch:**

Lunch Bunch is on a mission to change kids' nutrition and access to

knowledge about healthy eating - and ultimately influence the role food can play in

educating kids in a fun, creative, inspiring way. We are doing this by partnering with

schools to offer unique enrichment programming where food can be the foundation of not

only learning culinary arts & cooking, but also entrepreneurship, STEM skills, health and

fitness, world history and more. The curricula are thoughtfully designed to incorporate

multicultural learning, both familiar and growth mentality, partnership with school core

curriculums and long-term lessons to build healthy habits over a student's lifetime.

**Role Summary:**

The Administrative Coordinator role is responsible for maintaining accurate records,

supporting day-to-day administrative operations, coordinating communications, and

ensuring that internal systems and dashboards remain up to date.

While the primary focus of this role is administrative, the individual will also receive

cross-training in supervisory responsibilities to provide coverage when a supervisor is

unavailable. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, organized, proactive, and able to

understand how different departments work together to support overall operations.

**Responsibilities:**

Administrative operations, scheduling, supervisor coverage:

- Create and manage schedules, including coordinating coverage, filling open shifts, and updating schedules as needed.
- Coordinate with supervisors to address staffing needs and maintain smooth daily operations.
- Complete weekly exports and maintain accurate internal records.
- Update Paylocity cost centers, hiring and schedule dashboards, teacher onboarding sheets, and Airtable.
- Track outstanding tasks and ensure information is accurate and up to date.
- Prepare and distribute newsletters, announcements, reminders, and operational updates.
- Utilize scheduling software capabilities, and ensure all shifts are correct, accounted for, and all geo-fences are accurate
- Maintaining territory CRM
- Organize and manage teacher feedback, class photos, post-program surveys, and incident reports.
- Ensure teachers are completing feedback and surveys as data collection is important for the growth of the department/business
- Complete cross-training on supervisory workflows, systems, and procedures.
- Provide temporary supervisor coverage during absences, supporting routine operational tasks and scheduling needs

Requirements

- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and recurring responsibilities.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Proficiency with spreadsheets, digital databases, and administrative tools.
- Ability to learn new software, systems, and internal workflows quickly.
- Strong follow-through and accountability when managing assigned tasks.
- Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across departments.
- Sound judgment when identifying discrepancies, resolving routine issues, and escalating concerns.
- Flexibility and adaptability when shifting between administrative responsibilities and temporary supervisory coverage.
- Previous administrative, operations, or coordination experience preferred.

This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. The employee may be required to

perform other related duties as assigned to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.

individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

About LoanHQ
LoanHQ is a fast-growing business funding company located in the heart of Hollywood. We help small businesses access smart, flexible financing solutions—while keeping a fun, collaborative, “work hard, play hard” energy in the office.

We’re a small team that moves quickly, supports each other, and isn’t afraid to jump in wherever needed. If you’re organized, upbeat, and enjoy being part of a close-knit startup environment, you’ll fit right in.

Our office is easy to access, and we provide paid parking in an uncovered lot directly across the street for all on-site staff.

LoanHQ is an equal opportunity employer, and we provide reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants with disabilities.

We’re looking for a highly organized, friendly Office and Operations Coordinator who can support marketing efforts, client communication, and daily operational workflows. You’ll be central in keeping our client pipeline moving, supporting deals and making sure the team operates smoothly day to day.

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to grow with a company at the ground floor and build new skills in marketing, financial operations, CRM systems, and day-to-day business management.

Marketing & Client Support

Send emails, texts, and occasional scheduled phone calls as part of ongoing marketing campaigns

Contact clients to clarify documentation requirements and provide updates

Maintain accurate notes and follow-ups within the CRM

Operations Support

Communicate with funding partners to gather deal updates and requests

Assist with deal tracking, internal data accuracy, and document organization

Support leadership with administrative tasks within the scope of the role

Help coordinate vendor payments when needed

Office Coordination & Team Support

Keeping shared areas neat and organized

Picking up small trash items or emptying desk‑side wastebaskets into the main bin

$120.2k - $160.27k

Cumming Group

[Los Angeles, CA](https://jooble.org/jobs/Los-Angeles%2C-CA)

[Apply](https://jooble.org/away/8299641213613010749?p=1&pos=0&rgn=6546&pageType=7&jobAge=114&jdpSource=101&jdpid=-1230789072189855695&crId=US_0US_0)

Position Title:
Construction Scheduler

Location:
Los Angeles, CA

Time Type:
Full time

Description:
At Cumming Group, you will work on some of the world's most exciting projects in a dynamic environment where your success is measured by the impact you make. We are one of the fastest-growing project and cost management consultancies in the United States, as reflected in our top 15 rankings in ENR. With over 70 offices globally, an extremely diverse project portfolio, and double-digit year-over-year revenue growth, the opportunities to make your mark are limitless!

We are currently hiring a Construction Scheduler to support our Education sector projects. There are two positions available with one located in Woodland Hills and the other located in Wilmington, CA. This is a highly visible, high-impact role that will put you at the forefront of building the educational future for the Los Angeles community.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

Coordinate the preparation of project schedules based on defined project execution philosophies

Perform contractor schedule reviews for contract conformance and quality assurance

Evaluate contract change orders and amendments for impact on budget and schedule

Perform time impact analysis of project schedule delays and potential claims

Participate in change order negotiations

Perform Critical Path and Earned Value analyses

Identify schedule related problems which arise during project execution and recommend corrective actions and creative solutions

Conduct construction/project site visits for progress reporting

Review contractor’s weekly and monthly schedule progress, prepare narrative of findings, submit and present to management for decision making

Review and evaluate contractor recovery schedules

Perform cost analysis in support of design and construction phases of capital projects

Analyze actual expenditures versus budget performance

Prepare cost loaded schedule to support comprehensive cash flow projections

Understand, interpret and apply contracts, policies and procedures within the school district's guidelines.

Communicate effectively orally and in writing Excellent oral and written communication

Flexibility in schedule and transportation to work at multiple sites based on assigned schedule and duties

Ability to work in a fast-paced environment

Required Education and Experience:

10 years of experience in project or program scheduling on large construction programs

Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration or other related field. Additional qualifying experience in excess to the minimum stated above may be substituted for the required education on a year for year basis

Advanced proficiency in specified software including, but not limited to, Primavera Scheduling Software, MS Office Applications including Project, Excel, Word and PowerPoint

Knowledge of theories, principles and practices of cost engineering and scheduling

Experience with time impact analysis

Experience with construction claims and change orders

Flexibility in schedule and transportation to work at multiple sites based on assigned schedule and duties.

### Job Description Job Description S Y Lee Associates, Inc., an engineering consulting firm in Glendale, is seeking an organized, detail-oriented administrative professional with accounts receivable experience and a strong eye for document design. In this role, you will track client payments, follow up on outstanding balances, help our engineers prepare polished fee and technical proposals, and support daily office operations. The ideal candidate is comfortable working with numbers, persistent and professional in payment follow-up, and skilled at creating visually appealing business documents. Work Hours: Monday Through Friday, 12:00 - 5:00 PM Responsibilities - Accounts receivable: Track invoices, reconcile payments, and maintain accurate reports of outstanding balances. - Client payment follow-up: Proactively contact clients by email and phone regarding overdue invoices, request payment dates, track payment commitments, and keep management informed of unresolved balances. - Proposal preparation: Prepare, edit, and format fee and technical proposals using scopes, fees, and technical content provided by our engineers and management. - Document design: Create professional proposal layouts, covers, tables, graphics, and presentations. Maintain consistent company templates and proofread documents for accuracy, formatting, and visual quality. - Bookkeeping support: Assist with invoicing, accounts payable, bank deposits, and financial recordkeeping. - Office administration: Answer and screen calls, organize and archive emails, maintain files, and provide administrative support to management and project staff. Qualifications - Experience with accounts receivable, invoicing, bookkeeping, and professional client communication. - Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, especially Word, Excel, and PowerPoint including document formatting, spreadsheet formulas and reporting, presentation layouts, and email management. - Experience preparing professional proposals, reports, or presentations, with strong document-layout or graphic design skills. - Experience with QuickBooks and Sage/Peachtree. - Excellent written communication, organization, accuracy, and attention to detail. - Ability to handle confidential information, work independently, and manage multiple deadlines. Preferred Experience - Experience in an architecture, engineering, construction, or professional services office - Familiarity with website design

# Administrative Assistant

Oner Buttons

[Los Angeles, CA](https://jooble.org/jobs/Los-Angeles%2C-CA)

[Apply](https://jooble.org/away/199311492742393229?p=1&pos=0&rgn=6546&pageType=7&jobAge=90&jdpSource=101&jdpid=-7523994370742107416&crId=US_0US_0)

The Administrative Assistant will participate in day-to-day administrative and operational tasks for the Home Office Sales team. Assist with pre & post logistics for all sales, provide travel planning and expense reporting assistance and assist with on-boarding of new employees.

**The Career Opportunity**

The position will provide you with the exposure to operational tasks and opportunities for learning and further development.

**The Team / The Business**

The Administrative Assistant will be a member of the Sales team and will work closely with analysts and managers among various sectors and practices.

**Your Skills**

Excellent people skills, proactive, self-driven, strong communication (verbal and written) skills, social but professional demeanor. The Administrative Assistant will need to juggle and prioritize workload, be excellent at multi-tasking, be detail orientated and organized, and respond well to urgent requests while working in a fast-paced environment.

**Our Hiring Manager Says**

We are looking for the kind of person who is very organized and can multi-task. The kind of person who is a self-starter, a creative thinker, a problem solver and an independent worker.

**Responsibilities**

• Provide administrative support to the Ratings department with duties, including but not limited to, assisting with new hire on-boarding, preparing reports or proposals, filing, scanning, calendar management, expense reports, meetings and travel co-ordination.

• Work with Administrative Assistants in other regional offices on different presentations/bios/packages and special assignments.

• Assist in the coordination of meetings, action items and other administrative needs of the team, as required.

• Ensure team members are prepared for all meetings and carry forward action items.

• File management; keep current files on site, ensure all other files are either scanned and filed online or in offsite storage

• Act as an ambassador, plays a key role in ensuring that Oner is viewed as a professional, friendly, easily accessible and approachable partner internally and externally.

• Work cross functionally as part of a team with other members and departments.

Qualifications

• College or university degree preferred.

• 5+ years' experience in an administrative role ideally gained from banking, professional services or other fast-paced environments.

• Experience managing complex global travel arrangements and itineraries.

• Working knowledge of MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Calendar) and comfort and interest in learning new applications.

• Extremely motivated, eager to learn, adaptable and professional.

• Proven attention to accuracy and detail, highly organized with the ability to prioritize and multi-task.

• Exceptional (written and verbal) communication skills and interpersonal skills.

• Ability to work in a high performing culture, under pressure and with time-sensitive deadlines.

• Personable, easily interacts with all types of personalities and at all levels with a high degree of professionalism.

• Proven ability to work independently as well as to perform effectively in a team oriented environment

**Benefits**

Oner Buttons offers competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits and programs including: health and welfare, tuition assistance, 401K, employee assistance program, domestic partnership benefits, career mobility, employee network groups, volunteer opportunities, and other programs.

At Oner Buttons, We have been making quality and affordable buttons for quite some time. We originally only offered one-inch buttons hence our name "ONER". But as our business has grown we now offer an array of button sizes and options, as well as button packs. Just as before, we still pride ourselves on a 5-day or less turnaround on most orders. as well as prices to beat most other competitors.

Oner Buttons is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

# Administrative Assistant

Human Health Project Inc

[Los Angeles, CA](https://jooble.org/jobs/Los-Angeles%2C-CA)

[Apply](https://jooble.org/away/-8870675358056891586?p=1&pos=0&rgn=6546&pageType=7&jobAge=17758050&jdpSource=101&jdpid=-8665816078941435067&crId=US_0US_0)

Human Health Project (HHP) is a holistic health literacy charity. Our mission is to improve the health of the underserved and vulnerable through holistic information, education and advocacy. Our objective is to empower people to manage their own health with improved outcomes and no medical errors. For more information, please visit our website including viewing our "Shared Patient Information" program page which includes 50 pages of reports on both our Migraine and Lupus and feedback received from people who reviewed the reports in the section, "What Our Members are Saying" - and our "Healthcare Access Program" which includes short video courses in our Learning Academy - , Patient Advocacy Workshops in Los Angeles, - and in Northern Ireland - and our Online Peer to Peer Events - " Administrative Assistant Job Responsibilities: All work is virtual Provides administrative support to Human Health Project (HHP) CEO ensure efficient office operation. Answers phone calls and schedules meetings Carries out administrative duties such as filing, typing, copying, binding, scanning etc. Completes operational requirements by scheduling and assigning administrative projects and expediting work results. Exhibits polite and professional communication via phone, e-mail, and mail. Supports CEO by performing tasks related to organization and strong communication. Ensures operation of equipment by completing preventive maintenance requirements, calling for repairs, maintaining equipment inventories and evaluating new equipment and techniques. Provides information by answering questions and requests. Maintains supplies inventory by checking stock to determine inventory level, anticipating needed supplies, placing and expediting orders for supplies. Contributes to team effort by accomplishing related results as needed. Administrative Assistant Skills and Qualifications: Reporting Skills Administrative Writing Skills G-Suite Skills Microsoft Office Skills Managing Processes Organization Analyzing Information Professionalism Problem Solving Supply Management Inventory Control Verbal Communication Education and Experience Requirements High school diploma or equivalent education required 3 years of administrative assistant or similar experience Knowledge of appropriate software including: G-Suite, Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook, Microsoft PowerPoint and Adobe Acrobat Human Health Project Inc
